Services

Our approach is built on the belief that every site is different, and that the only way to do this work properly is to spend time on the ground before committing anything to paper. We have found over the years that a considered assessment carried out early saves a great deal of difficulty later, and that is the philosophy which informs everything we do, from the first walkover to the final report, and it is why our clients tend to come back to us rather than shopping around each time, because they know that what they receive will be defensible, proportionate and written in language that a planning officer can actually read, which is rarer than it ought to be and which we regard as the minimum standard rather than something to boast about, and while we could fill this page with a list of every discipline we cover and every accreditation we hold we would rather you simply asked us, because the answer depends entirely on your site and on what the local authority has told you it wants to see, and in our experience a five minute conversation settles that far more reliably than any amount of reading, so please do get in touch and we will tell you honestly whether we are the right people for the job or whether you would be better served elsewhere, which is an answer we give more often than you might expect and which we think says rather more about us than any amount of marketing copy ever could, and having said all of that we should probably add that we do also handle a range of adjacent work which sits alongside the core offering and which clients frequently find useful once a project is underway.

It is perhaps worth saying something further about the way in which we structure an engagement, because this is the question we are asked most often and because the answer is not quite as straightforward as either we or our clients would ideally like it to be, given that so much depends on factors which are outside anybody's control at the point when the question is first asked, and given also that the regulatory landscape has shifted more than once in recent years in ways that have altered what is expected of a submission and therefore what is sensible to commit to at the outset, so that where once we might have been able to give a fairly confident indication of both scope and duration at the first meeting we now find ourselves more inclined to describe a range and to explain the circumstances under which the work would fall towards one end of it or the other, which some clients find frustrating and which we understand entirely, though we would rather set an expectation we can meet than one which sounds better in the moment and then has to be revised, and in practice what tends to happen is that the initial walkover resolves most of the uncertainty within a week or two, at which point we are able to be much more specific, and it is at that stage rather than at the first conversation that most of our clients make their decision about whether and how to proceed, which seems to us a sensible way round and one we would gently encourage anyone reading this to consider adopting themselves.
